Condo buildings in Central Lonsdale
Georgian Manor (also marketed as "The Georgian") — 140 East 20th Street (City)

Built 1971; 14 units. A listing for a unit in the building describes it as a freehold, 14-unit mid-century walkup that allows pets (2 cats) and rentals, with strata fees including heat and hot water. The building-directory name is Georgian Manor; the listing text calls the building "The Georgian" — one building, counted once. Published age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Victoria Park West — 160 West Keith Road (City)

Built 1996; a concrete building beside Victoria Park (listings state 15 storeys). Unit count: Not confirmed. The building directory states pets allowed with restrictions and rentals not allowed — the "rentals not allowed" line is void for long-term rentals since November 24, 2022.
The Grande — 160 East 13th Street (City)

Built 1999 by Bosa; a concrete building with a live-in caretaker, gym, amenity room and workshop per current listings. Unit count: Not confirmed. The building directory states pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed with restrictions — read the filed bylaws for what the rental restriction actually says, because a long-term rental ban itself would be void.
Ridge Park Gardens — 2059 Chesterfield Avenue (City) — 55+

Built 1995 (the building directory and current listings state 1995; one listing states 1996 — 1995 governs). A 55+ community: listings state "one owner must be 55+" and describe an adult-oriented (55+) building with a guest suite, clubhouse, workshop, gardens and greenhouse, and one listing states the building allows 2 cats or 1 dog and 1 cat. Unit count: Not confirmed. The building directory states age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions, and rentals not allowed — the "rentals not allowed" line is void for long-term rentals since November 24, 2022, but the 55+ age bylaw is the one age bylaw BC law still allows.
Anderson Walk — 119 West 22nd Street (addresses 119–152 West 22nd Street) (City)

Built 2012 by Polygon; a 5-storey wood-frame development of 234 units per the developer information sheet, with a fitness centre, residents' lounge and guest suite. The building directory states pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed.
Centreview — 112 East 13th Street (project address 1308 Lonsdale Avenue) (City)

Built 2017 by Onni Group; listings state Freehold Strata title and describe a concrete tower one block off Lonsdale with concierge and 10,000+ sq ft of amenities including a heated outdoor pool, hot tub, fitness centre, squash court and guest suites. The project source states 17 storeys and 114 homes. Published rental, pet and age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Millennium Central Lonsdale — 135 East 13th Street (City)

An 18-storey mixed-use tower by Millennium Development Group with ground-level retail and healthcare office space; the presale source states 172 condominiums plus 8 laneway townhomes, with estimated completion 2025, and the project marketing source lists the status as Complete with units actively listed as brand-new, move-in-ready homes. Published rental, pet and age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Lennox (Lennox on Lonsdale) — 110 East 17th Street (City)

By Polygon Homes; the presale source states a 6-storey mixed-use wood-frame building with 64 condominiums and 17,000 sq ft of commercial space, with expected completion June 2025; current listings state year built 2026 and show Polygon Realty selling the final homes. Sources differ on the completion year (presale estimate versus listings). Published rental, pet and age restrictions: not confirmed.
Elle — 128 West 15th Street (presale address 132 West 15th Street) (City)

By Polygon Homes; a 22-storey mixed-use tower with a 2-storey podium, 136 condominiums including 38 adaptable suites, estimated completion 2026 per the presale sources, with current listings stating year built 2026. Published rental, pet and age restrictions: Not confirmed.
Streets, schools and getting around Central Lonsdale

items.t: Central Lonsdale is the City of North Vancouver's own name for the Lonsdale Avenue corridor core: the mixed-use blocks along Lonsdale Avenue around 13th to 23rd Streets, with Lions Gate Hospital, City Hall, the City Library and the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre inside or at the edge of the area. The City's Lonsdale Great Street project area extends from the Upper Levels Highway to Victoria Park and from St. Georges Avenue to Chesterfield Avenue; full neighbourhood street-by-street limits beyond that project area are not verified. City-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 8400 (2014, amended December 8, 2025).

Condo stock actually concentrates on and immediately beside Lonsdale Avenue between 13th and 23rd Streets and on the numbered cross-streets one block east and west of it (13th Street East/West, 15th Street, 17th Street, Keith Road, 20th–22nd Streets, Chesterfield Avenue and St. Georges Avenue) — that is where every verified building in sits.

Nearby areas: Lower Lonsdale and Lonsdale Quay / the Shipyards (south, down Lonsdale Avenue to the waterfront), Upper Lonsdale (north, up Lonsdale Avenue past Highway 1 into the District), Grand Boulevard / Boulevard (east), and Mahon Park / Norgate (west).

Main streets and transit: Lonsdale Avenue is the spine — south to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus (12 minutes to Waterfront Station, every 15 minutes during the day), north to the Highway 1 interchange. TransLink route 230 runs the full length of Lonsdale Avenue through Central Lonsdale, from Lonsdale Quay to Upper Lonsdale; the R2 RapidBus runs east–west on 3rd Street / Marine Drive at the area's south edge and since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Anchors inside the area: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street; North Vancouver City Library, 120 West 14th Street; Queen Mary Community Elementary, 230 Keith Road West; Carson Graham Secondary, 2145 Jones Avenue, at the north end; and the Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre, main entrance 130 East 23rd Street, which opened Saturday, July 25, 2026 with an NHL-sized arena, a 25-metre pool, steam room, sauna, hot pools, fitness area and a full-sized gymnasium (at opening the aquatics centre was still in final checks and health-authority approvals, expected ready for fall programming).

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Lonsdale

items.t: The hospital, the library and the new recreation centre are all inside this one sub-area. Lions Gate Hospital at 231 East 15th Street, the City Library at 120 West 14th Street and the Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre at 130 East 23rd Street (opened July 25, 2026) all sit on the Central Lonsdale grid — but at the recreation centre's opening the aquatics centre was still in final checks, testing, staff training and health-authority approvals, expected ready for programming and lessons in the fall, so a possession-date promise of pool access in summer 2026 would have been wrong.
The corridor's cheapest-looking building is not a strata at all.

Two of the corridor's directory "bans" are legally dead, one age rule is alive. The "rentals not allowed" lines at Victoria Park West and Ridge Park Gardens cannot bar a long-term tenancy since November 24, 2022 — but Ridge Park Gardens' 55+ rule is the one age bylaw BC law preserves, and it still governs who may occupy the unit.

The density rewrote itself on December 8, 2025. City-wide, single-detached dwellings fell from 20% of total units in 2001 to 11% in 2021 while apartments in buildings of five or more storeys rose from 15% to 29% (Statistics Canada 2021, via the City's census backgrounder), and the GO Zone adopted December 8, 2025 then raised permitted units to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties — Central Lonsdale is where that shift is concentrated, and its side-street lots now price on OCP designation, not on the old single-family zoning.

The next tower is already named, priced as a presale, and three years out. One20 (Three Shores, 21 storeys, 164 condominiums) is set to welcome residents in June 2028 — a buyer comparing it against the completed 2025–2026 towers is comparing a REDMA presale against finished strata stock, with GST, completion risk and rescission rights all differing accordingly.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Central Lonsdale

Municipality, stated first because it decides the bylaws: Central Lonsdale is in the City of North Vancouver — OCP Bylaw No. 8400 / Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995). The District of North Vancouver's OCP 7900 / Zoning 3210 belong to the District (Delbrook, Norgate and their neighbours) and are never imported here.
The Beeches — West 13th Street (address carried as 230 West 13th Street from the listing below). Strata

Court reporting on the complex's strata dispute describes "The Beeches townhouse complex on West 13th Street," a block from City Hall, and records that its strata council took a short-term-rental matter to the Civil Resolution Tribunal, with a September 2017 order against the owner — strata tenure is therefore evidenced by the strata council and CRT record itself, not by marketing. A listing for a unit at 230 West 13th Street records Sub-Type Townhouse, built 1980, wood-frame construction, with strata amenities (maintenance grounds, management, snow removal). Unit count: Not confirmed — no source checked states it, and the exact civic address range for the whole complex is likewise not confirmed beyond the listed unit's address. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: Not confirmed — confirm on the Form B; the reported dispute was about short-term rentals, which a strata may still restrict by bylaw.
Streets, schools and getting around Central Lonsdale

items.t: Central Lonsdale is the City's own name for the Lonsdale Avenue corridor core: the mixed-use blocks along Lonsdale Avenue around 13th to 23rd Streets, with Lions Gate Hospital, City Hall, the City Library and the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre inside or at the edge of the area. The City's Lonsdale Great Street project area extends from the Upper Levels Highway to Victoria Park and from St. Georges Avenue to Chesterfield Avenue; full neighbourhood street-by-street limits beyond that project area are not verified. City-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan, 2014, Bylaw No. 8400, amended December 8, 2025 (Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9114) for provincial housing requirements.
Both statements are carried; neither is upgraded.

Central Lonsdale is in the City of North Vancouver, which is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's FVR + GVR September 2026 reports — no North Vancouver section, sub-area rows or community medians exist for it, and no other stats source is substituted. All market figures for this area: Not verified.
The one counted townhouse complex sits on West 13th Street, a block from the avenue.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 230 runs the full length of Lonsdale Avenue from Lonsdale Quay to Upper Lonsdale; the R2 RapidBus runs east–west on 3rd Street / Marine Drive at the area's south edge and since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station; the SeaBus at Lonsdale Quay crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Central Lonsdale

items.t: Form B diligence (the 1 counted strata complex, and every apartment strata documented above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Chesterfield Manor has no Form B — share-ownership diligence is the corporation's own documents, a different process entirely.

Fee-simple homes (the side-street house stock): Note the middle form documented: a home can look detached and still sit in a bare-land-style small strata (the 3-home Bewicke Avenue strata) — the title, not the built form, decides which diligence applies.

City zoning and plan — the CITY pair only: Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 8400 (2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995). Side streets sit in the Ground Oriented (GO) Zone adopted December 8, 2025: a lot of 280 m² or less allows up to 3 units, a lot over 280 m² allows up to 4 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation and up to 6 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4 designations; the GO Zone increased permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 residential properties and allows up to 6 units per lot on approximately 600 properties. One secondary suite is permitted per single-family property (owner must reside at the property), and a suite may combine with an accessory coach house where the front lot line is at least 10 m, with a Development Permit and Building Permit.

Great Street plan: Council approved the Lonsdale Great Street Plan on April 20, 2026 — a 20-year vision for the Central Lonsdale main street, with the first phase of public-space improvements underway in 2026, funded by the Province's Growing Communities Fund.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Lonsdale

items.t: The corridor's one counted townhouse complex is famous for a court case, not its floorplans. The Beeches' strata spent years and, per the reporting, about $25,000 in legal bills fighting a townhouse used as a 16-bed hostel a block from City Hall; the CRT ordered the use shut down in September 2017 and the courts rejected the owner's petitions in May of the following year as reported. A buyer inherits that strata's short-term-rental enforcement posture — and its legal-cost history is a Form B and minutes question, not a listing question.

The hospital, the library and the recreation centre are all inside this sub-area. Lions Gate Hospital at 231 East 15th Street, the North Vancouver City Library at 120 West 14th Street, and the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre at 130 East 23rd Street (opened July 25, 2026, with an NHL-sized arena and a 25-metre pool; at opening the aquatics centre was still in final checks, expected ready for fall programming) — that cluster is the product the corridor sells.
The cheapest-looking building on Chesterfield is not a strata at all.

The City sized its December 2025 updates to a stated housing need: 21,301 units over 20 years on top of its existing 29,021 units, in a city of 58,120 people on 11.83 km² (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, via the City's census backgrounder) — the density context behind the GO Zone and the Harry Jerome Neighbourhood Lands, where Lonsdale Square rental and a seniors' residence are already built on part of the lands.

The elementary catchment is about to move. SD44's new Cloverley elementary school opens for 2026/27 and the catchment review potentially moves Queen Mary catchment addresses east of Lonsdale Avenue — a 2025 catchment promise may not hold for a family writing in 2026.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Lonsdale
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established side-street house lots: ground-oriented houses, duplexes and multiplexes on the side streets under the Ground Oriented (GO) Zone, with strata condos and apartments in low-, mid- and high-rise buildings on and beside Lonsdale Avenue, the North Shore's most urban mix. The avenue and side-street pattern is historic subdivision fabric: built lots, not a lot offering. The strata/freehold split by street is not confirmed.

Lot character, as the City states it: GO Zone subdivision minimum lot width is 7.5 m in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation (10.0 m for a corner lot) and 15.0 m in other designations; older bylaw minimum lot areas include 464.5 m² in RS-2 and 334.4 m² in RS-3. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Serviced position: the corridor sits inside the City's serviced urban system — the City's own subdivision instrument (Bylaw 8014) regulates and requires the provision of works and services for subdivision and development; parcel-level servicing detail for a specific lot: Not verified — confirm with the City. A City single-family utility fee total for 2026: Not verified.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Central Lonsdale is documented; parcel-level ALR status is listed not verified there. No ALR percentage split is stated — check any specific parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping.

items.t: : The City states these are City lands planned for housing in high-rise and ground-oriented forms, with Lonsdale Square and a seniors' residence already built on part of the lands and further lands to be made available by the City; the developer for future phases is not verified on the City page. This is a municipal land-planning position, not a lot offering: no lot count, no lot sizes and no sale terms are published in the material read, and nothing here is carried as for-sale inventory.

Lonsdale Great Street Plan (approved by Council April 20, 2026): a 20-year vision to strengthen and revitalize Central Lonsdale as a vibrant neighbourhood main street, protecting its local businesses, active sidewalks and diverse community while planning for future growth, with the first phase of public-space improvements underway in 2026 — a public-realm plan that shapes avenue-front land value; it creates no lots and is not a development offering.

items.t: Roads and transit: Lonsdale Avenue is the spine — south to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus, north to the Highway 1 (Upper Levels) interchange at the top of the City; Keith Road and the numbered streets are the east–west links. TransLink route 230 runs the full length of Lonsdale Avenue through Central Lonsdale, from Lonsdale Quay to Upper Lonsdale; the SeaBus at Lonsdale Quay crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day; the R2 RapidBus runs east–west on 3rd Street / Marine Drive at the area's south edge and since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic anchors inside the area: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street; North Vancouver City Library, 120 West 14th Street; Victoria Park on Lonsdale Avenue at Keith Road; Mahon Park — the City's largest park, running parallel to Jones Avenue — at the west side; and the Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre, main entrance 130 East 23rd Street, which opened Saturday, July 25, 2026 (at opening the aquatics centre was still in final checks and health-authority approvals, expected ready for fall programming). A grocery store name and address in the core confirmed on an official source: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Lonsdale

items.t: OCP / Zoning — CITY rulebook only: City of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, 2014, Bylaw No. 8400 (amended December 8, 2025, Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9114, for provincial housing requirements) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995).

GO Zone density (adopted December 8, 2025): a lot of 280 m² or less allows up to 3 units; a lot over 280 m² allows up to 4 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation and up to 6 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4 designations; the adoption increased permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 residential properties and allows up to 6 units per lot on approximately 600 properties. The City sized its December 2025 updates to a 20-year housing need of 21,301 units on top of its existing 29,021 units. Subdivision minimum widths are in.

Subdivision + servicing — the City's own instrument, verified on the City source: the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw, 2010, No. 8014 (consolidated June 14, 2021) is "a Bylaw to regulate and require the provision of works and services in respect of the subdivision and development of lands and to establish the standard of services to be provided" — applicants for subdivision and building permits are required to provide the works identified in its Schedule A unless otherwise provided by Development Variance Permit. The City's process runs from a Preliminary Application (which expressly covers new lots, lot-line adjustments, airspace parcels, bare land strata and phased strata plans, submitted to subdivision@cnv.org) to final approval, with final fees calculated by City staff after preliminary review, based on bylaw fees and the actual cost to service the proposed lot configuration.

Streamside hazard: the City's Streamside Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 15 metres of the top of bank of a watercourse or within 10 metres of the top of a ravine bank, and a development permit is required before new development there — relevant near the Wagg Creek and Mahon Park ravine lands at the area's west side. Parcel-level floodplain status: Not verified.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Central Lonsdale ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of the land's value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Lonsdale

items.t: The City rewrote this area's land math on December 8, 2025: the GO Zone adopted that day raised permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties and allows up to 6 units on about 600 — a side-street lot's value now turns on its OCP designation (Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 vs 2 / Residential Level 4), not on its old single-family zoning, and the same day's OCP amendment (Bylaw 9114) was made for provincial housing requirements against a stated 20-year housing need of 21,301 units.

The City has legalized suites here since 1993: secondary suites have been permitted in all single-family dwellings in the City since 1993 — the suite position on an older Central Lonsdale house lot is a long-standing right with an owner-residency condition, not a new SSMUH experiment.

The City's own census backgrounder shows the density shift: city-wide, single-detached dwellings fell from 20% of total units in 2001 to 11% in 2021, while apartments in buildings of five or more storeys rose from 15% to 29%, and Central Lonsdale is where that shift is concentrated. The City's 2021 Census population was 58,120 on 11.83 km² (Statistics Canada 2021, via the City's census backgrounder).

blocks.text: New construction in Central Lonsdale, North Vancouver

items.t: New construction homes for sale in Central Lonsdale, North Vancouver

faq.a: On and one block off Lonsdale Avenue between 13th and 23rd Streets. The nine verified buildings in run from Georgian Manor (1971) and The Grande (1999) through Anderson Walk (2012) and Centreview (2017) to the 2025–2026 Polygon and Millennium product (Lennox, Elle, Millennium Central Lonsdale) — the corridor is the City's densest condo stock, and the side streets beyond the avenue blocks are GO Zone houses, duplexes and multiplexes.
faq.q: Where in Central Lonsdale do condos actually exist?

faq.a: Yes for a long-term tenancy — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022, whatever the older directory lines at Victoria Park West and Ridge Park Gardens still show. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind.
faq.q: A directory says my building bans rentals. Can I still rent my unit out long-term?

faq.a: The published evidence says yes in the legally valid form: listings describe a 55+ community and state "one owner must be 55+," and the directory records age restrictions. Only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, from May 1, 2023, younger spouses/partners and defined children — confirm the filed bylaw wording on the Form B.

Tenure. The directory and the listing also conflict on pets (directory: pets not allowed; listing: 1 cat or dog up to 35 lbs allowed). Specialist legal and financing review is required before treating it as interchangeable with a strata purchase.
faq.q: Chesterfield Manor looks like the cheapest condo on the corridor — what is the catch?

faq.a: No. It is a purpose-built rental building (built 2024, 113 units, 6 storeys) on the Harry Jerome Neighbourhood Lands — there is no strata lot to purchase. The same lands hold the new recreation centre (opened July 25, 2026) and further City lands planned for housing in high-rise and ground-oriented forms.
faq.q: Is Lonsdale Square a condo building I can buy into?

faq.a: One named standalone complex is verified here: The Beeches on West 13th Street (strata, with a unit listing recording built 1980). Everything else townhouse-form is either a component inside an apartment strata (Millennium's 8 laneway townhomes, Vista Place's ground units) or an unnamed small side-street strata.
faq.q: Where are the actual townhouse complexes in Central Lonsdale?

faq.a: Different strata, different diligence, different comp set.
faq.q: Are Millennium's laneway townhomes a townhouse complex I can comp against The Beeches?
Is there a 55+ townhouse in Central Lonsdale?

faq.a: The City of North Vancouver's Lonsdale Avenue corridor core — the shops and services around 13th–17th Streets, Lions Gate Hospital, City Hall and the City Library, the new Harry Jerome recreation centre at the north end, and the residential side streets between St. Georges and Chesterfield Avenues.

Queen Mary Community Elementary (K–7), 230 Keith Road West, is inside the area and Carson Graham Secondary (8–12), 2145 Jones Avenue, is at its north end; catchments are address-based, and SD44's new Cloverley elementary school (opening 2026/27) may change elementary catchments east of Lonsdale — check the exact address with SD44.
faq.q: Which schools are located in Central Lonsdale?

faq.a: Route 230 buses run down Lonsdale Avenue to Lonsdale Quay, where the SeaBus crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes; the R2 RapidBus on 3rd Street / Marine Drive now runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay to Metrotown.
faq.q: How do you commute downtown from Central Lonsdale?
